Ethan B.: Hey folks, first-day snag. I'm on Linux Mint (NetworkManager + systemd-resolved) using the company OpenVPN split-tunnel profile. VPN connects, I can SSH to bastion by IP, but internal hostnames like `registry.internal.redwood` fail to resolve from my shell and from Docker. `curl http://registry.internal.redwood/health` returns: `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: registry.internal.redwood`. Any BYOD-safe unblocks?
Priya (infra-oncall): welcome Ethan! this is a classic systemd-resolved + split-tunnel issue. Quick test: `resolvectl status` and `systemd-resolve --status` will show which DNS servers are active. What does `resolvectl status` show for your VPN interface?
Ethan B.: output shows only my home resolver on `wlan0`. The tun0 (VPN) interface is up but no DNS entries. I tried adding `10.12.5.10 registry.internal.redwood` to `/etc/hosts` and `curl` works, but `docker login registry.internal.redwood:5000` still times out.
Marco (devex): Docker uses its own resolver chain depending on setup; adding to `/etc/hosts` helps CLI tools but Docker daemon may not pick it up. Two quick options: 1) SSH port-forward the registry through the bastion, or 2) make the VPN push DNS for split-tunnel (infra ticket). Which do you want now?
Ethan B.: need to pull onboarding image asap, port-forward sounds fastest. How?
Priya (infra-oncall): run from your host: `ssh -L 5500:registry.internal.redwood:5000 ethan@bastion.redwood.internal -N`. Then `docker login localhost:5500` and `docker pull localhost:5500/redwood/onboarding:latest`. We'll whitelist your public IP for the bastion tunnel while onboarding. Reply with `@IT Support Bot whitelist` to get temporary allowlist.

Ethan B.: forwarding worked, `docker login localhost:5500` succeeded and I pulled the image. Thanks! A follow-up though: I want hostnames to work from my shell and WSL-like containers without always port-forwarding. Any safe steps I can take on my Mint laptop?
Marco (devex): if you want a local permanent-ish fix without changing system trust: one approach is to let NetworkManager trigger a dispatcher script that writes the VPN-provided DNS into `/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf` or into `/etc/resolv.conf` depending on your config. Example dispatcher script `/etc/NetworkManager/dispatcher.d/99-vpn-dns` (requires sudo):
```
#!/bin/bash
IFACE="$1"
STATUS="$2"
if [ "$IFACE" = "tun0" ] && [ "$STATUS" = "up" ]; then
  # pull DNS from nmcli and write resolv.conf
  DNS=$(nmcli -f IP4.DNS connection show --active | awk '/IP4.DNS/ {print $2; exit}')
  echo "nameserver $DNS" | sudo tee /etc/resolv.conf
fi
```
Make it executable and NetworkManager will run it when the VPN comes up. Caveat: this modifies resolv.conf and might interfere with your home network when VPN is down.
Ethan B.: I don't want to risk breaking normal browsing. Any non-invasive tweaks?
Priya (infra-oncall): alternative minimal change: set DNS only for split-tunnel by using `nmcli connection modify <vpn-conn> ipv4.dns "10.12.2.2" ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes` and then `nmcli connection up <vpn-conn>`. That instructs NetworkManager to use the corporate DNS for that connection only, leaving your general DNS intact when VPN is disconnected. If you're unsure, we can do it together over a quick screen share. I'll also file INF-4347 to push the split-tunnel profile to include DNS for BYOD clients.
Ethan B.: prefer the nmcli approach, does it require root?
Marco (devex): yes you'll need sudo to modify the connection. Command example: `sudo nmcli connection modify "Redwood VPN" ipv4.dns "10.12.2.2" ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes && sudo nmcli connection up "Redwood VPN"`. Test `resolvectl status` afterwards.
Ethan B.: did the nmcli tweak, `resolvectl status` now shows the corporate DNS on tun0 and hostname resolution works from shell. Docker daemon still used old resolver for some reason.
Priya (infra-oncall): Docker may cache DNS or be using systemd-resolved stub. Restart the docker daemon: `sudo systemctl restart docker` so it picks up the updated `/etc/resolv.conf`.
Ethan B.: restarted docker, now `docker login registry.internal.redwood:5000` works without the tunnel. Great.
Priya (infra-oncall): marking this thread as INF-4347 followup for infra to push DNS into split-tunnel profile + doc update. If anyone prefers not to modify their connection, SSH port-forward remains the recommended onboarding unblock.
Ethan B.: huge help, thanks everyone. I'll leave the temporary hosts entry removed and keep the nmcli change. Appreciate the quick responses. :rocket:
